subject: Warning in cor(x, y) : the standard deviation is zero

messages.author: 855455c89480e6f5
messages.subject: Warning in cor(x, y) : the standard deviation is zero
parts:
Hi Wallace Team,

I'm running a maxent model using L, LQ, H, LQH feature classes and regularization multipliers in the 0.5-4 range increasing by 0.5. I have 23 occurrence records and 10,000 background points randomly sampled. 

I'm getting several warnings in the R console saying: Warning in cor(x, y) : the standard deviation is zero. When I go to the evaluation table some of the fields (for example cbi.val.avg and AICc) have NA Values.

Can anyone help me with what this warning means and if I shouldn't consider models with NA evaluation fields when selecting the best model?

Thanks a lot!
Daniela

messages.author: fe049c2835236bb1
messages.subject: Re: Warning in cor(x, y) : the standard deviation is zero
parts:
Hi Daniela,

I find this error often happens when there are few occurrence records, high complexity features, and low regularization, which are all the ingredients to get a very complex model. If you get NA for AICc, that means there were more non-zero coefficients (model parameters) than you have occurrence records, which violates the assumptions of AIC. If you're using AIC for model selection, just ignore this model. You may also get NA for validation CBI because if there are not enough records in the training data during cross-validation, CBI will return NA -- this occurs with small datasets. I would just ignore it and use a different metric like omission rate or AUC.

Jamie
